_note: What the briefer researches, by account type. This is docs/research-agenda.md section 2.2 as data: edit the agenda and this file together. `standard` is the highest evidence tier a question normally allows (government, regulator, company, press). `required` questions must be answered or reported as a gap. Nothing here has been tested against live sources.

questions.ask: Legal name, charter and regulator, holding company, headquarters, size, ownership (public, private, mutual), and any pending merger.

How much commercial real estate by category (multifamily is its own Call Report line; hotel and retail are not separate), how much is past due or non-accrual by category, the trend over eight quarters, and how that compares with peers. For a public bank, the credit-quality tables in the 10-K and 10-Q, which sometimes break out hotels and retail.
where: FFIEC and FDIC Call Report data and UBPR

questions.ask: Has the bank said it will sell, reduce or exit commercial real estate or problem loans? Has it sold loans before, to whom, and through which advisor?
where: recorded assignments of mortgage and UCC-3 assignments (past loan sales, and who bought)

questions.ask: Any consent order, written agreement, memorandum of understanding or prompt-corrective-action status, or any enforcement action naming the institution.
where: FDIC, OCC and Federal Reserve enforcement databases

questions.ask: Confirm who holds the decision for the kind of debt we want, and that the named person holds the role. Title keywords by department: special assets, workout, managed assets, recovery, OREO, credit resolution (non-performing loans); secondary marketing, whole loan, loan sales, loan syndications, capital markets (performing pools, participations, whole-loan sales); chief credit officer, chief lending officer, senior credit officer (at a smaller bank often the decision-maker); the president. Title, tenure, prior roles, public speaking, associations. Two dated sources. A name on a recorded affidavit, assignment of mortgage or court declaration is good evidence of the role, but it concerns a particular asset, so mark it asset-specific.
where: recorded assignments of mortgage, notices of default and court declarations (the officer who signed)

questions.ask: Who advises or represents the bank (counsel, loan sale advisor, title officers, auditors)? Outside counsel named in foreclosure, receivership and bankruptcy filings is often the fastest warm path.
Next earnings date, recent leadership change, conferences the named person will attend.
Loans or properties publicly tied to the bank in a court or regulatory record. CONTEXT ONLY, never for a message.
Any reason not to approach now: receivership or imminent failure, an active sale process run by an advisor, an adverse enforcement action against the named person.
Parent company, ownership, special servicer ratings, offices, scale.
What they special service by property type and size, and recent transfers, as far as public trust reports show.
where: SEC filings for CMBS trusts (10-D, ABS-EE)

questions.ask: How they resolve loans (note sales, REO sales, discounted payoffs), which advisors they use, who buys.
Confirm the named person's role and tenure, and find the heads of asset management for our sectors. Two dated sources.
The controlling class or directing certificateholder on trusts they manage, where public.
An active process with a named advisor, litigation or a rating action that would make an approach unwelcome.

fund.label: Debt fund, mortgage REIT, bridge lender or other lender

questions.ask: Type, sponsor, size, strategy, listing status.
Loan book by property type, non-accrual and sold-loan disclosures, maturities, securitization or CLO structure.
Stated plans to sell or resolve non-performing loans, and who they sold to.
Confirm the named person's role; find heads of asset management, workouts and credit. Two dated sources.
Any reason not to approach now (active process, litigation, regulatory action).
Firm, office, practice group, and the partners who handle receiverships and foreclosures.
Public dockets: receivership or foreclosure filings by state and sector, for which lenders, with which receivers.
Bar status and any public discipline for the named lawyer.
The named partner's role, publications, speaking, associations.
Appointments by court, sector and year, and the counsel and lenders they work with.
Firm, principals, sectors, states, licensing where required.

broker.label: Loan sale advisor or note broker

questions.ask: Firm, sectors, geographies, principals; confirm the named person's role.
Public closed-deal and offering announcements: size, sector, lender type.
Which lenders and servicers they act for, where public.
